item.title: Do Life Insurance Companies Lend in Secondary and Tertiary Markets? What Actually Changes Outside the Top 25 MSAs
item.description: Life companies lend in smaller markets every quarter. What changes is the underwriting: leverage drops 5 to 10 points, debt yield floors rise, and the asset has to be the best of its type in the market. Here is the real framework, dial by dial.

item.title: Pittsburgh Commercial Real Estate Market Update: Week of July 20, 2026
item.description: For the week of July 20, 2026, Pittsburgh's capital markets are navigating a cautiously constructive rate environment alongside a notable bifurcation in lender appetite, with medical office and industrial corridors drawing competitive terms while downtown office continues to test borrower patience.

item.title: Sacramento Commercial Real Estate Market Update: Week of July 20, 2026
item.description: For the week of July 20, 2026, Sacramento-area borrowers are navigating a rate environment where spread compression on agency multifamily is running ahead of broader market expectations, while Elk Grove industrial refinances are surfacing a basis problem that is reshaping how lenders are sizing proceeds on 2021 and 2022 vintage acquisitions.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Damyan

item.title: Portland Commercial Real Estate Market Update: Week of July 20, 2026
item.description: For the week of July 20, 2026, Portland-metro commercial real estate borrowers are navigating a rate environment that has stabilized but not softened, with lender appetite sharply bifurcated by submarket and property type as capital sources continue to price in Oregon's regulatory friction alongside deal-specific fundamentals.

item.title: San Antonio Commercial Real Estate Market Update: Week of July 20, 2026
item.description: For the week of July 20, 2026, San Antonio's commercial real estate debt markets are navigating a modestly firmer rate backdrop alongside tightening lender scrutiny on new multifamily supply, while industrial and medical office product along key corridors continues to attract competitive capital from multiple lender types.

item.title: Orlando Commercial Real Estate Market Update: Week of July 20, 2026
item.description: For the week of July 20, 2026, Orlando's commercial real estate capital markets are navigating a moderately constructive rate environment alongside persistent lender selectivity, with Lake Nona medical office and last-mile industrial along the SR-528 corridor drawing the clearest execution this week.

item.title: Charlotte Commercial Real Estate Market Update: Week of July 20, 2026

item.title: Life Company vs. Debt Fund: How They Actually Price a $10M to $25M Value-Add Deal
item.description: Most comparisons frame this as picking one lender. The sophisticated capital stack for a value-add deal in the $10M to $25M range uses both, sequenced correctly, with the debt fund carrying execution risk and the life company taking out the stabilized asset.
